page: Amazon Web Services r5.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, providing 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 64.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU acceleration, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent throughput in memory-bound execution alongside modest compute capacity. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 50.08 GB/sec with write speeds of 35.76 GB/sec, supporting average performance in data stores with 6.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 2,735.12 PassMark database operations. Conversely, raw processor performance falls within lower benchmark quartiles, reflected in single-threaded gzip compression at 21.84 GB/sec and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3,969.0.

The instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for architectures requiring substantial RAM footprint per CPU core without necessitating bleeding-edge computational speed. The absence of bundled local disks necessitates networked storage solutions for stateful data. The hardware profile is aligned with in-memory caching layers, relational databases, search index caching, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r5.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. It features no local disk storage, no GPU hardware, and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves average memory and caching throughput, recording 50.08 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 6.73 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core and compression performance test in lower tiers, reflecting an architecture prioritized for memory density over raw compute speed. This resource allocation provides efficient hardware utilization for memory-heavy setups such as in-memory caches, distributed databases, search indexes, and enterprise batch pipelines.
